title: Three Sum
statement:
You are given an array of n integers. Find every distinct triplet of values that adds up to zero.

Two triplets are the same if they contain the same three values, regardless of where those values sat in the array. Each distinct triplet is reported once.

Sort the three values inside every triplet in ascending order. Then sort the triplets themselves in ascending order, comparing the first value, then the second, then the third.
inputFormat:
Line 1: the integer n, the length of the array.
Line 2: n integers, the array. This line is absent when n is 0.
outputFormat:
Line 1: the integer k, the number of distinct triplets.
Then k lines, one triplet each, three values separated by single spaces, in the order described above.

When k is 0, print only the line holding 0.
sampleNotes: The triplets are (-1, -1, 2) and (-1, 0, 1). The array holds -1 twice, so (-1, -1, 2) is available, but it is still reported only once.
No three values add up to zero, so the answer is 0 and nothing follows it.
hint: Sort the array first. Then fix the first value and walk two pointers inward from both ends of the rest. Skipping over repeated values is what keeps each triplet from being reported twice. Trying every triplet is n cubed, which takes about four seconds on the largest test and will not fit in the limit.

starter.py:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]

# Your code here. Print k, then the k triplets.
